def-kauffman-regular-isotopy-and-dubrovn:
## Definition

Let
$$R_D=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1})),$$
where $z$ is not inverted. A nonempty unoriented regular link diagram is a
finite generic planar projection of one or more circles with only transverse
double crossings and an over/under marking at each crossing. Use the crossing
chart in which the over-strand runs southwest to northeast. Its $D_0$
smoothing joins the left endpoints and the right endpoints (the through
pairing), and its $D_\infty$ smoothing joins the two top endpoints and the two
bottom endpoints (the cup-cap pairing). Thus $D_0$ is the orientation-preserving
smoothing when both crossing strands point downward and the displayed crossing
has positive determinant sign. These are respectively the $A$- and
$B$-smoothings in the stated bracket chart. A positive
curl is a type-I kink whose oriented crossing has determinant sign $+1$; a
negative curl has determinant sign $-1$. The sign is unchanged if the
orientation of the whole component is reversed.

The Dubrovnik regular-isotopy evaluation $P$ is normalized by
$P(\varnothing)=1$, $P(K\sqcup\bigcirc)=dP(K)$, positive and negative curl
factors $a$ and $a^{-1}$, and
$$P(D_+)-P(D_-)=z\bigl(P(D_0)-P(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
Here $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ only by switching the displayed crossing. For a
nonempty oriented link diagram $K$, let $c(K)$ be its number of components and
let $w(K)$ be the sum of the determinant crossing signs. Define
$$D_K(a,z)=d^{-1}P(K),$$
$$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ),\qquad i^2=-1,$$
and
$$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z).$$
Thus $D$ has unknot value $1$, and the universal relation defining $R_D$ is
retained even when $z$ is not invertible. These are conventions and
normalizations; ambient-isotopy invariance of $F$ is a separate theorem.
def-bmw-dubrovnik-coefficient-extension:
## Definition

Let
$$S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$$
be the universal Dubrovnik coefficient ring. Define the coefficient extension
$$T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z).$$
Inside $T$ write $z_B=q-q^{-1}$, $z_D=z_B$, $\rho=a$, and $\delta=d$. These names specify the intended BMW and Dubrovnik parameter images; the compatibility of their coefficient relations is proved separately.
lem-kauffman-dubrovnik-writhe-component-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For each nonempty oriented regular link
diagram $K$, let $w(K)$ be its determinant writhe and $c(K)$ its number of
components, and define $D,L,F$ by the conventions stated for this page. Then
$$D_K(a,z)=-i^{-w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}L_K(ia,-iz),\qquad i^2=-1.$$
The value assigned to $L$ is independent of reversing the orientation of any
whole component. The Dubrovnik value has the stated difference-skein, curl and
circle rules; the Kauffman value has the sum-skein, curl and circle rules; and
$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z)$ is unchanged by planar isotopy and every oriented
Reidemeister move of types I, II, and III. The claim concerns these finite
diagram moves and uses the universal coefficient relations without dividing
by a skein variable.
lem-bmw-relations-dubrovnik-parameter-di:
## Statement

Let
$$S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$$
be the Dubrovnik coefficient ring, and let
$$T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z).$$
In $T$ put $\rho=a$, $\delta=d$, and $z_B=q-q^{-1}$. Then the natural
map $S\to T$ is injective and $T$ is a free $S$-module with basis $1,q$.
Moreover, the BMW coefficient relation
$$z_B(\delta-1)=\rho-\rho^{-1}$$
holds, and the substitution $a=\rho$, $z_D=z_B$, $d=\delta$ converts
the BMW skein, curl, adjacent untwisting, and loop coefficients to the
Dubrovnik relations in the specified chart: $D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$,
the curl factors are $a,a^{-1}$, and a disjoint trivial circle contributes
$d$. Here $D_0$ is through and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap. No skein parameter is
divided out.
def-dubrovnik-tangle-skein-algebra:
## Definition

Fix $n\ge0$ and a rectangle with $n$ distinct ordered endpoints on its top edge and $n$ on its bottom edge. An ordinary $(n,n)$ tangle diagram is a finite generic planar projection in the rectangle of arcs joining these endpoints and finitely many closed curves, with an over/under marking at each transverse double point and no other singularities. Two diagrams are regularly isotopic when related by planar isotopy fixing the boundary and Reidemeister moves II and III. Their regular-isotopy classes form a monoid under vertical stacking, with the $n$ straight strands as its identity. In the fixed crossing chart, $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ by switching the marked crossing, $D_0$ is the through left/right smoothing, and $D_\infty$ is the cup-cap top/bottom smoothing. The displayed $D_+$ has its over-strand running southwest to northeast; with both strands directed downward it is the determinant-positive Artin crossing. A positive curl is a type-I kink with determinant crossing sign $+1$; a negative curl has sign $-1$. Define $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ to be the $T$-algebra obtained from the monoid algebra of these classes by imposing, in every interior disk, the Dubrovnik relations
$$D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty),\qquad \text{positive curl}=a\,\text{straight strand},\qquad \text{negative curl}=a^{-1}\,\text{straight strand},$$
and the free-circle relation that adjoining one disjoint circle with no crossings with the tangle multiplies it by $d$. The symbols $a,z_D,d$ are the images from the coefficient extension. No type-I move is imposed as a regular isotopy; its effect is represented by the displayed curl relations.
lem-bmw-presentation-tangle-evaluation-i:
## Statement

Let $T$ be the coefficient extension and parameter substitution in the BMW-to-Dubrovnik dictionary, and let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra: its diagrams are finite generic projections of $n$ arcs with fixed ordered top and bottom endpoints and closed curves, modulo planar isotopy, Reidemeister II and III, the Dubrovnik skein relation, the two curl relations, and the free-circle relation with parameters $z_D,a,a^{-1},d$. In its fixed chart, $D_0$ is through left/right and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap top/bottom. For every $n\ge2$, send the BMW generator $g_i$ to the positive Artin crossing between strands $i,i+1$, its inverse to the negative crossing, and $e_i$ to the adjacent cup-cap tangle. This assignment extends to a unital $T$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi_n:BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta)\to\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$. For $n=0,1$, define the unital $T$-algebra homomorphism by sending each scalar to that scalar times the empty or straight tangle, respectively. This claim asserts well-definedness only; it does not assert surjectivity or injectivity.
lem-bmw-descending-tangle-spanning:
## Statement

For each integer $n\ge0$, let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$, with $z_D=q-q^{-1}$. Let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra formed from regular-isotopy classes with crossing rule $D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$, curl factors $a,a^{-1}$, and free-circle factor $d$, where $D_0$ is through and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap. Number its $2n$ boundary endpoints in cyclic order as $1,2,\ldots,n,\bar n,\ldots,\bar2,\bar1$. A connector is a perfect matching of these endpoints. Orient each open strand from its lower-numbered endpoint to its higher-numbered endpoint and order the open strands by their initial endpoints. Place the finitely many closed strands after the open strands in any fixed order, with a chosen orientation and initial point for each. A diagram is totally descending if, in this traversal order, the first branch encountered at each crossing is the overpassing branch. Then $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ is spanned by one loop-free, self-crossing-free totally descending tangle for each connector. These representatives can have crossings between distinct strands; their crossing data are fixed by the total traversal order. For $n=0$ the single representative is the empty tangle, and for $n=1$ it is the straight strand.
lem-bmw-finite-source-normal-form-over-d:
## Statement

Let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$. Put $\rho=a$ and $\delta=d$. For every $n\ge0$, the abstract presented algebra $BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta)$ has a finite basis indexed by the perfect matchings of $2n$ endpoints. In particular it is spanned by $N_n$ elements, where $N_0=1$ and $N_n=(2n-1)!!$ for $n\ge1$. This is a source-module assertion about the generators-and-relations algebra, independently of any proposed map to a Dubrovnik tangle algebra.
lem-bmw-closure-pairing-independence:
## Statement

Let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and let $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$. For each $n\ge0$, index the standard descending matching tangles by the perfect matchings $m$ of the $2n$ boundary endpoints. Reflect a second such tangle across the horizontal midline and glue corresponding boundary endpoints to obtain a closed diagram. Let $M_n$ be the matrix whose $(m,m')$ entry is the scalar Dubrovnik evaluation $P$ of this closure. Then $\det M_n$ is nonzero in $S$, its image is a non-zero-divisor in $T$, and the standard matching tangles are linearly independent over $T$. The assertion is over this universal coefficient extension and makes no independence claim after an arbitrary nonflat specialization.
lem-bmw-markov-trace-stabilization:
## Statement

For $n\ge1$, let $\Phi_n$ be the BMW-to-Dubrovnik tangle homomorphism over $T$, let $\widehat{t}$ denote closure of an $(n,n)$ tangle by joining corresponding top and bottom endpoints without a twist, and define
$$\tau_n(x)=d^{-n}P\!\left(\widehat{\Phi_n(x)}\right),\qquad x\in BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta).$$
Then $\tau_n$ is a cyclic $T$-linear trace, compatible with the tower inclusion $\iota_n:BMW_n\to BMW_{n+1}$ that adds one straight strand, and for every $x\in BMW_n$,
$$\tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x))=\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)g_n)=a d^{-1}\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)g_n^{-1})=a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)e_n)=d^{-1}\tau_n(x),$$
where $a=\rho$ and $d=\delta$.
lem-bmw-descending-tangle-spanning-and-i:
## Statement

Over the universal coefficient extension $T$ from the BMW-to-Dubrovnik parameter dictionary, for every $n\ge0$ the natural map $\Phi_n$ from the presented BMW algebra to the Dubrovnik $(n,n)$ tangle skein algebra is an isomorphism. Both algebras are free $T$-modules on the standard totally descending, loop-free, self-crossing-free matching tangles indexed by perfect matchings of the $2n$ boundary endpoints. The common rank is $(2n-1)!!$ for $n\ge1$, with rank one at $n=0$ and $n=1$.
alg-kauffman-polynomial-from-bmw-braid-c:
## Definition

Use the coefficient extension $T$ with $a=\rho$ and $d=\delta$. On input an integer $n\ge1$ and a finite signed Artin braid word
$$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m},\qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{-1,1\},\quad 1\le i_j<n,$$
perform the following finite computation:

1. Form the BMW product $b_\beta=g_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots g_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m}$.
2. Set $w=\sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_j$ and let $c$ be the number of cycles of the permutation $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_m}$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, counting fixed points.
3. List the perfect matchings of the $2n$ tangle boundary endpoints and their standard descending representatives $T_m$. For each signed generator, form its finite left-multiplication matrix in this basis: its column at $T_m$ is obtained by reducing the tangle $g_i^{\pm1}T_m$ to the unique matching coordinates. In each reduction, use the standard endpoint traversal order, choose the first crossing whose first traversal branch is under, and with $\eta=1$ for the fixed $D_+$ chart and $\eta=-1$ for its crossing-switched $D_-$ chart replace
$$R(D)=R(D^{\mathrm{sw}})+\eta z_D\bigl(R(D_0)-R(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
The switched branch has one fewer non-descending crossing, and each smoothing has one fewer crossing; a descending leaf is reduced by the curl and free-circle rules to its standard matching representative. Starting with the coordinate vector of the identity tangle, apply the generator matrices from the rightmost braid letter to the leftmost to obtain the coordinate vector $v_\beta$ of $\Phi_n(b_\beta)$.
4. Form the trace row $t_m=d^{-n}P(\widehat{T_m})$ by closing each basis tangle and evaluating its scalar Dubrovnik value, and return
$$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(b_\beta).$$

Here $\tau_n(b_\beta)=t^{\mathsf T}v_\beta$. The output is the declared Kauffman ambient-isotopy value at $A=ia$, $Z=-iz$ in the Dubrovnik parameter convention. All matrices are finite and all coefficients lie in $T$; no division by the skein variable is used.
thm-bmw-markov-trace-gives-dubrovnik-inv:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every nonempty oriented link $K\subset S^3$ and every finite signed Artin braid word $\beta$ whose oriented closure represents $K$, the corrected BMW trace value
$$Q(\beta)=-(-1)^{c(\beta)}a^{-w(\beta)}d^{n-1}\tau_n(\beta),$$
where $n$ is the strand count, $c(\beta)$ is the number of closure components, and $w(\beta)$ is the determinant writhe, is independent of the braid representative. It equals the declared writhe-normalized Kauffman ambient-isotopy invariant of $K$ at $A=ia$, $Z=-iz$.
thm-kauffman-polynomial-from-bmw-braid-c:
## Statement

For every admissible input consisting of an integer $n\ge1$ and a finite signed Artin braid word with indices $1\le i<n$, the BMW braid-closure algorithm terminates after finitely many algebra and skein reductions and returns exactly
$$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(\beta).$$
Here $w$ is the determinant writhe of the oriented closure, $c$ its component count, and $\tau_n$ is the normalized scalar closure trace. This theorem asserts no parser behavior for invalid inputs and no asymptotic complexity bound.
thm-kauffman-and-dubrovnik-conversion:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a nonempty oriented link with determinant writhe $w(K)$ and component count $c(K)$, and let $Q_K$ be the value returned by the BMW braid-closure algorithm for any finite signed braid word representing $K$. Then $Q_K$ is independent of the chosen braid and
$$Q_K=F_K(ia,-iz)=-(-1)^{c(K)}a^{-w(K)}D_K(a,z),$$
equivalently,
$$D_K(a,z)=-i^{-w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}L_K(ia,-iz),\qquad i^2=-1.$$
The proof covers the unknot, positive and negative curls, and both self-crossing split and mixed-crossing merge smoothing cases under the stated universal coefficient relation, without dividing by $z$.
